s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of immobility, mutism, and systemic stiffness with abdominal distension and altered mental status
salient_findings: Mute with vacant stare and no eye contact
key_facts: 56-year-old female
History of diabetes mellitus
History of mental illness diagnosed in 1998
Stable on quetiapine for many years
Developed new symptoms including stupor in 2016
Condition deteriorated in November 2017
Abdominal distension and tympany on physical exam
Absent bowel sounds on physical exam
No guarding or rigidity of abdomen on physical exam
Bilateral rigidity on neurological exam
Mental status: mute with vacant stare and no eye contact
Hypomagnesemia and hypokalemia on laboratory tests
Abdominal CT showed accumulated air and fecal matter, dilated intestine with air-fluid levels
Brain CT and MRI showed no remarkable findings

shortlist.label: Malignant catatonia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms of immobility, mutism, and systemic stiffness with altered mental status are consistent with malignant catatonia

shortlist.label: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: History of quetiapine use and development of new symptoms including stupor and systemic stiffness are consistent with neuroleptic malignant syndrome

shortlist.label: Catatonic schizophrenia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's history of mental illness and current symptoms of catatonia are consistent with catatonic schizophrenia

shortlist.label: Paralytic ileus
shortlist.why_kept: Abdominal distension, tympany, and absent bowel sounds are consistent with paralytic ileus

shortlist.label: Hypokalemic paralysis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's laboratory results showing hypokalemia and symptoms of muscle weakness and paralysis are consistent with hypokalemic paralysis

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including stupor, abdominal distension, absent bowel sounds, bilateral rigidity, and a high Bush-Francis Catatonia Rating Scale score, are consistent with malignant catatonia. The presence of hypomagnesemia and hypokalemia also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome
rejected.why: Although the patient was on quetiapine, the absence of fever and the presence of abdominal distension and absent bowel sounds are not typical of neuroleptic malignant syndrome

rejected.label: Catatonic schizophrenia
rejected.why: The patient's history of mental illness and stability on quetiapine for many years, followed by a sudden deterioration, suggests a more acute condition than catatonic schizophrenia

rejected.label: Paralytic ileus
rejected.why: While the patient has abdominal distension and absent bowel sounds, the presence of air-fluid levels on abdominal CT and the patient's mental status changes are not typical of paralytic ileus

rejected.label: Hypokalemic paralysis
rejected.why: Although the patient has hypokalemia, the presence of abdominal distension, absent bowel sounds, and a high Bush-Francis Catatonia Rating Scale score are not typical of hypokalemic paralysis

gold: Schizophrenia with catatonic features and chronic intestinal pseudo-obstruction (CIPO)
